messages:
Nina Patel: Hi team — need help. We're finalizing an international adoption (Russia). Child's arrival is next week but passport and US SSN won't be ready for several weeks. Can we get temporary coverage and an ID letter to show at the pediatrician? Hospital may bill before docs are in.
Riley Foster: Congrats! We can provisionally enroll the child for medical only pending paperwork. Required provisional docs: adoption placement letter from agency, court filing receipt (if available), travel/immigration papers, and parent IDs.
Nina Patel: I have the placement letter and travel docs only. What's the fastest way to get a proof letter?
Benefits Bot: Generated temporary dependent coverage letter (ID ADP-441). Valid for 30 days. It confirms provisional medical coverage effective on arrival date provided in the placement docs. Link: https://internal.benefits.redwood/letters/ADP-441
Nina Patel: Thank you! What file formats and naming help processing?
Riley Foster: PDF preferred. Filename: empID_lastname_adoptplacement_date.pdf (e.g., 54321_Patel_adoptplacement_20260315.pdf). Upload to Benefits Portal > Dependent Docs > International Adoption.
Nina Patel: One more — payroll asked whether premiums start immediately or wait until SSN and birth record are in.
Payroll Bot: Payroll policy: provisional enrollments trigger coverage for claims but premium deductions begin after Benefits confirms enrollment in system. If finalized retro to arrival date, payroll will run a pro-rated adjustment.
Carrier Rep - UnitedCare: For billing, please include claim note "ADOPT-INTL" and attach ADP-441. If the provider bills before final docs, submit itemized invoice and we'll attempt direct payment/explanation of benefits. Expect initial carrier response within 72 hours.
Nina Patel: Uploading placement letter now. Appreciate the quick turnaround — especially with a pediatrician appt on Thursday.
Riley Foster: Marked as expedited. We'll follow up after carrier ACK. :thumbsup:
